pulse.label: Domestic Mill Supply
pulse.basis: SMU reported shrinking remaining 2026 domestic spot tonnage for plate and sheet, with steel buyers struggling to find domestic mills offering spot availability. This indicates tightening spot access, not a measured decline in total U.S. plate production.
pulse.limitation: Qualitative buyer reports; cannot infer exact mill allocation percentages or all-grade availability. Supply direction here refers to domestic spot-order availability.

sources.title: Sheet and plate price gains accelerate as 2026 tons dry up

pulse.label: Mill Lead Times
pulse.basis: SMU's late-October buyer survey reported that sheet and plate mill lead times continued to lengthen; plate exceeded its 2021 peak and set a record for its survey series beginning in 2018. Its October 16 report placed average plate lead times at 11 weeks.
pulse.limitation: Survey-based U.S. market trend, not a guaranteed lead time from any specific plate mill, grade or thickness. The 11-week average was reported October 16, not October 29.

sources.title: Mill lead times climb to new highs, buyers expect little relief

imports_detail.product: Cut-length carbon steel plate (not aggregate steel imports)

developments.summary: AISI reported August cut-length plate import permits rose 72% versus July final imports. Permits are intended tonnage, not confirmed arrivals or currently available plate. September broad steel imports do not establish a later cut-length plate trend.
developments.limitation: Do not infer import availability is improving from permits alone; check subsequent cut-length plate arrivals and comparable permit data.

source.title: AISI Releases August SIMA Imports Data

imports_detail.method: Licenses and permits indicate potential incoming volume, not landed inventory. Compare the same plate product definition across successive months and distinguish preliminary licenses from final Census arrivals. No directional conclusion is drawn from one month or from all-steel totals.

demand_drivers.name: Energy, oil & gas
demand_drivers.grades: A516 Grade 70 for specified vessels; A36 / A572 Grade 50 for skids and supports
demand_drivers.analysis: Tanks, separators, process vessels and heavy equipment can consume discrete plate. Oil prices and drilling activity are indirect indicators; funded fabrication orders, specification requirements and project timing matter more than announcements.

sources.scope: Indirect; not plate tonnage or transaction prices
sources.title: Short-Term Energy Outlook
sources.summary: EIA’s dated outlook projects a lower Brent price next year; this is an energy forecast, not a plate forecast.

demand_drivers.name: Power generation & data centers
demand_drivers.scope: Selected direct plate applications; much demand is for other products
demand_drivers.grades: A36 / A572 Grade 50 skids and baseplates; A516 Grade 70 where pressure equipment specifications require it
demand_drivers.analysis: Generator skids, tanks, baseplates and selected power equipment provide a plate channel. Building frames, rebar, electrical steel and many enclosures belong to different product markets. Electricity-demand projections do not establish plate tonnage; grid access and project execution can delay consumption.

sources.title: United States Data Center Energy Usage Report: 2025 Update
sources.scope: Electricity-demand scenarios; not a plate demand forecast
sources.summary: DOE/LBNL research projects substantial data-center electricity-demand growth with a wide scenario range. It does not estimate carbon steel plate tonnage. The forecast treats demand for selected power equipment, tanks and generator skids as a conditional plate channel; building frames and other steel products are distinguished.

demand_drivers.name: Infrastructure
demand_drivers.scope: Plate bridges and equipment versus structural products
demand_drivers.grades: A36 / A572 Grade 50 where project specifications permit
demand_drivers.analysis: Bridge fabrication, heavy equipment and selected industrial structures can create plate orders. Many projects primarily use beams, rebar or other steel. Funding must turn into procurement before it becomes current plate demand.

accuracy.summary: Not yet evaluable. No completed forecast quarter has a sufficiently verified, like-for-like plate outcome. No accuracy score or actual price has been invented.

rules: Red / ↑ = increasing pressure. Orange / → or ↔ = stable or mixed. Green / ↓ = easing pressure. Gray / — = insufficient or expired evidence. Colors do not mean good or bad.

Only explicit dated discrete-plate directional observations qualify. Low inventories, strong demand levels, all-steel production and aggregate imports cannot establish a change in plate supply or demand.

Recognized producer quarterly plate-price direction is eligible for 45 days from period end, at Low confidence. Other reviewed observations default to 30 days unless their record documents a different window. Future dates and expired observations are excluded.
Conflicting eligible readings on the same evidence date show Mixed at Low confidence. Missing data never defaults to Stable.

Daily snapshots preserve evidence and readings. The weekly baseline is the latest saved snapshot on or before seven days ago, no more than fourteen days old. Missing weeks are not backfilled. Coverage changes are separate from physical market changes.

Mill webpages are checked daily, but only recognized or reviewed dated developments are shown. A planned outage end is never treated as a confirmed restart. Capabilities pages do not verify current operations or allocations.

Forecast accuracy needs a completed quarter and reviewed like-for-like observations for discrete plate. A current-quarter forecast requires the matching remaining-period baseline; a full-quarter result cannot substitute. Coil/HRC, all-steel output, within-quarter price changes and unverified headlines do not qualify. No suitable automated actual-price series is configured.
